patch_description:
The original implementation failed validation because it could alter dataframe structure and row/cell alignment during recursive reconstruction. In particular, it created dataframes from raw `.values.tolist()`, overwrote rows using completion-order futures, added and removed an `original_index` column, merged discarded columns back by value, and finally sorted rows independently of the returned column ordering. This could duplicate, misalign, reorder, or lose original values. It also returned an empty column-ordering list despite performing per-row column permutations.

The replacement keeps every original cell, row, column, index, and shape intact. It normalizes values only for scoring, builds a bounded set of candidate column-order strategies, selects the strategy using the actual serialized-string Trie/LCP objective, and returns valid per-row column orderings. Column merge groups are treated as contiguous ordering blocks and one-way dependencies are respected as ordering precedence constraints.
